newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr steady vs yen, eases vs mark in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr steady vs yen, eases vs mark in Tokyo.

text.p: 0533 GMT -- *Dollar steady against yen but eased versus mark in afternoon Tokyo trade.
*Dollar supported versus yen by short-covering interest by interbank players, but upside seen capped at around 113 yen by hedge-selling interest from trust banks and exporters.
*Tokyo operators cautious ahead of release of Japan's current account data for April on Wednesday.
*Some players see possibility of dollar dipping below 112 yen if current account surplus is bigger than expected.

*Reuters poll of economists showed, on average, that Japan's April current account surplus would grow to 1.13 trillion yen, compared with a surplus of 566.6 billion yen last year. The forecasts ranged from 990 billion yen to 1.21 trillion yen.
*Mark/yen edged higher but upside seen capped by Japanese exporters' selling interest.
*Mark stood at around 66.17/20 yen at 0537 GMT, up from around 66.08 yen at midday.
*Mark seen remaining susceptible to worries about European economic and monetary union (EMU), dealers said.
0300 GMT -- *Dollar was steady by Tokyo midday on Tuesday due to buy-back interest by overseas speculative funds and public and private institutional investors, traders said.
*Buy-back came after Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka called recent forex movements excessive and said Japan will deal appropriately with excessive currency moves.
*Dollar's recovery against the yen from early lows was also helped by a large quantity of sterling purchases for the yen by a major local brokerage firm.
